chapter_theme: The dawning of knowledge (ஞானோதயம்): Siva is not known by his colour or form but in knowledge he himself gives, through the path of the worthy and the guru; the seeker who searches for 'I' and 'He' is shown they are not two. Images of a lamp lit within a lamp, of gems and of nectar mark the knowledge, which is called the path of nadanta, true yoga and release.
structure_note: Bliss in the states (2813); the Lord known by service and knowledge, not sight (2814, 2815); the lamp, the tattvas, the nectar and the gems (2816 to 2819); 'I' and 'He' not two (2820); the good path of knowledge (2821 to 2824). The grouping is mine; 2821 to 2823 each repeat an opening phrase.

2813.reading: What the mind sees at its juncture is the mind's waking; seeing bliss as dream comes, and, on inquiry, the ceasing beyond it, are called bliss; Nandi, who has reached his own, says bliss is twofold.
2813.nuance: மனசந்தி (the juncture of the mind), மனநனவு (the mind's waking) and மீதொழிவு (the ceasing above) are technical terms of the states of consciousness that I can't fix. Which two blisses are meant (perhaps the bliss seen in a state and the bliss of its ceasing) is not stated plainly; இனமுற்றான் is obscure.

2814.reading: My Lord, whose hand killed the elephant, who holds a skull in his hand and wears the burning young crescent: I only became his servant, calling him rare and great; whether he is dark or red I cannot see.
2814.nuance: The first two lines give Siva's familiar marks (the flayed elephant, the skull-bowl, the crescent), and the last line refuses to describe him: devotion came without knowing his colour. கரியன்கொல் சேயன்கொல் (is he dark, is he red) may also hint that he is neither Mal nor any visible form.

2815.reading: The exalted one who drank the poison so that the great might drink nectar grants, if you enter by the path of austerity the worthy have taught, a knowledge like refined gold; seek it by the way of the Naked One's feet.
2815.nuance: நக்கார் சுழல்வழி is obscure. I take நக்கர் as the Naked One (a name of Siva) and சுழல் as a variant of கழல் (anklet, the feet), but it may be 'the whirling way of those who laugh'. தக்கார் (the worthy) points to the guru and the line of teachers.

2816.reading: For those who can split the lamp, light the lamp, trim the lamp within the lamp and make the lamp shine in the lamp, reaching the feet of the Lord who owns the lamp becomes possible.
2816.nuance: The whole verse plays on விளக்கு (lamp), also 'to make clear'. It is traditionally read of the soul's light kindled by the guru's knowledge until it shows the Lord's light within; splitting the lamp may be the separation of soul from bonds. The plain riddle and the symbolic reading both stand.

2817.reading: Where the tattvas are, the Lord of the tattvas is there; where the tattvas are not, he is not there; once one knows the nature of knowledge of the tattvas, the Lord himself appears there.
2817.nuance: தத்துவன் may be the Lord who rules the tattvas, or 'the Real' as against தத்துவம் (the real things). The second line seems to deny the Lord where there are no tattvas, which may mean he is reached only through knowing them, or be wordplay that the last line resolves.

2818.reading: Within the true knowledge that holds up the sky, what wells up from the spring becomes rare nectar; on his spreading matted hair, shining like fresh gold, he stands joined with the scent of the safflower.
2818.nuance: அசும்பு (oozing, a spring) and the nectar it yields are traditionally the fluid felt to flow from the crown in yoga. விசும்பு ஒன்று தாங்கிய may be knowledge that bears the inner sky. The link between the nectar and Siva's fragrant hair is not stated.

2819.reading: The light that dwells in the cosmos of souls, like pearl, diamond, coral of the sea, clustered fresh gold and pure-shining ruby: in what way will you call it different and divide it?
2819.nuance: The gems are not alike, yet each shines; the question argues that the one light is not to be split by the many forms it shines in. ஒத்து உயிர் அண்டத்துள் can also be read 'matching, within soul and cosmos'.

2820.reading: I searched, calling it 'I' and calling it 'He', and as I searched, the First of knowledge who is the 'I' granted me that 'I' and 'He' are not two; and I, the one who said 'I', ceased to think.
2820.nuance: நான் and தான் (I and He, or I and the self) are the two terms; the knowledge that they are not two is given (நல்கினான்), not reached. The verse can be read as plain non-duality or, as Siddhanta reads such verses, as inseparability without identity; it says இரண்டில்லை and no more.

2821.reading: The good path of knowledge is the good path of nadanta; the good path of knowledge is knowing it as 'I'; the good yoga of knowledge is standing in the good state; the good release of knowledge is the Veda of nadanta.
2821.nuance: நாதாந்தம் (the end of nada) is one of the six ends (ஆறந்தம்). நன்மோகம் is odd: மோகம் is delusion or longing, and I read it as standing for மோக்கம் (release); the text may be corrupt. நானென்று அறிவோர்தல் echoes 2820.

2822.reading: For those who can be saved, Siva-knowledge is their life; Siva the god is their life; Om is where they dissolve; and they become the knowing within knowing.
2822.nuance: ஒடுக்கம் (withdrawal, dissolution) makes the syllable Om the place into which the saved are drawn back, not only a sound they recite.

2823.reading: To those who can see, he is like the pupil of the eye; to those who can see, like nectar from the sea; to those who can cherish him, Nandi, the great name, never fails; to those who can hold fast, he becomes their support.
2823.nuance: ஆணவல்லார் is obscure: it may mean those who can hold fast or rule themselves, or, by a pun, those free of ஆணவம் (the root impurity). The nectar of the sea recalls the churning, when Siva drank the poison (2815).

2824.reading: Like the sound that stands within the letter Om, the excellent thing the gods above desire is the feet of our Lord, the red flame standing far off; the gods who seek them become his inner retinue.
2824.nuance: The sound within Om is traditionally the nada beyond its letters. அகம்படி (inner retinue, palace attendants) may also mean that the feet become the seekers' inner dwelling.

links.note: Both verses are built on repeated விளக்கு (lamp): in 1818 lighting the lamp lets one know the open space and those who light it shine in it; in 2816 the lamp lit within the lamp leads to the feet of the lamp's owner.
2815 names the churning, Siva taking the poison so the gods could drink nectar; 2823 turns that nectar into what Siva himself is to those who can see.

46 has devotees naming the Lord by colours, அந்திவண்ணா, முந்திவண்ணா, while the one who enters the mind is புந்திவண்ணன், the one coloured as the intellect. 2814 carries this further: the poet became his servant calling him rare and great, but cannot say whether he is dark or red (கரியன்கொல் சேயன்கொல் காண்கின்றிலேனே). Together they show colour-names as the devotee's speech, not a seen attribute.

2817 says that once the nature of tattva-knowledge is known, the Lord of the tattvas appears there (தத்துவன் அங்கே தலைப்படும்); 2666 uses the same words (தத்துவன் தன்னைத் தலைப்படலாம்) but makes the way cutting the many bonds and contemplating beyond thought (நினைப்பற உள்கில்). 2666 adds conditions to 2817's knowledge: reaching the தத்துவன் also needs the bonds cut and thinking stilled.

2819 asks how one can call the light dwelling in all, like pearl, diamond, coral, gold and ruby, different and divide it (எத்தன்மை வேறென்று கூறுசெய்வீரே); 104 says the three gods, examined, are one in continuity, and the world quarrels dividing them (பேதித்து உலகம் பிணங்குகின்றார்கள்). Both rebuke division of the one: 2819 through the many gems, 104 through the three gods.

Near-repeat. 2820 (நான்என்றும் தான்என்றும் நாடினேன் ... இரண்டில்லை ... நல்கினான்) and 1441 (நானென்றும் தானென்றும் நாடி ... இரண்டிலாத் தற்பதம் ... நல்கலால்) both search 'I' and 'He', are granted that they are not two, and end with the 'I' falling silent. 1441 ends 'I cannot speak of He and I', 2820 'I ceased to think': the same experience told as loss of speech and as loss of thought.

Kural 346 says one who cuts off the pride of saying 'I' and 'mine' (யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு) enters a world above the gods. 2820 goes past cutting pride: after the gift that 'I' and 'He' are not two, even the 'I' that said 'I' ceases to think (நான்என்ற நானும் நினைப்பு ஒழிந்தேனே). The Kural's renunciation of the ego is carried to its disappearance in knowledge.

2821 names the good path of knowledge as the path of nadanta and its release as the Veda of nadanta (நாதாந்த வேதமே); 2386 joins Vedanta and Siddhanta as one seal and lists bodhanta, yoganta and nadanta with bliss rising when one sinks into silence. 2386 sets 2821's nadanta within the full scheme of the six ends, showing it as one of them rather than the whole path.

2822 says Om is the place of dissolution (ஒடுக்கம் பிரணவம்) for those who can be saved; 2676 says within Om are the one word, form and formless and many distinctions, and Om is bright release and attainment (ஒண்முத்தி சித்தியே). 2676 explains why Om can be the saved ones' ஒடுக்கம்: everything is held within it.

source_issues: 2823: line 3 reads பேணவல் லார்க்கப் பிழைப்பிலன், apparently for பேணவல்லார்க்கு அப் (or லார்க்குப்) பிழைப்பிலன்.
2821: நன்மோக in line 4 may be a corruption of நன்மோக்க (release); as printed it reads 'good delusion'.
